extracted.intended_audience: aspiring novelists, literary critics, and students of fiction
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on the craft of the novel: how to shape time, point of view, method, and form so a book achieves unity of design and the intended dramatic/pictorial effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters with lives beyond the book / realism of persons
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters should seem to have 'evident lives of their own' beyond the limits of the book; they must be intelligible and familiar so readers can easily extend their lives in any direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure characters are consistent and true to themselves; avoid making their reality depend solely on exotic or eccentric presentation. Realism may come either from an author's special angle (Balzac) or from absorbing everyday experience so fully that characters feel familiar (Tolstoy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of space and of daylight
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuity of space and daylight is necessary to the motive of a book and must be rendered consistently to sustain the novel's effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain coherent spatial and temporal continuity appropriate to the novel's aims so the setting supports, rather than distracts from, the larger design.

rubrics_metrics.name: The form of time must be represented
rubrics_metrics.description: If time is of the essence of the book, 'the form of time is to be represented' — not merely the sequence of events but the movement and shape of time itself in the book's structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the lines and masses of the whole book (structure, pacing, placement of episodes) to make the passage of time perceptible rather than relying on mere announcements or lists of events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show both uninterrupted lapse and cyclic sweep of time
rubrics_metrics.description: Time in a novel has two effects: its steady progression (uninterrupted lapse) and the rise-and-fall or cycle of which the chosen stretch is part; both must be made present where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render daily, gradual changes (faces, gestures, thought) as well as the larger generational or cyclical movements; ensure the narrative gives a sense of the wheel’s circumference even if only a segment is shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mastery of changes of age and the effects of time on character
rubrics_metrics.description: A novelist should convey how men and women grow older and change with 'noiseless regularity,' preserving sameness amid mutability so that time's effects feel authentic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track subtle shifts in manner, thought, and appearance through the years; make time readable in characters' faces, gestures and the changing texture of their thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design / moral embedded in the form
rubrics_metrics.description: The picture of events must have a design: 'the moral is in its design,' and without design scattered scenes will make no coherent picture or meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide the broad effect or reason for telling the story and shape chapters and episodes so they collocate to express that design rather than remaining a series of unconnected scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening and closing must frame the story's promise and conclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel's start should set the right impression and promise; its end should gather threads and present a final shape so that lives reach a discernible conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct openings that immediately establish the story's movement and climactic/terminal episodes that tie together major threads; avoid an ending that feels arbitrary or that leaves the central form unresolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a fixed subject and consistent purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: The novelist should fix the subject and the design in mind; vacillation in intention or method weakens the book's ability to express a single, broad effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine the novel's central subject and retain that guiding intention throughout composition; changing the intended view midstream will scatter value and diminish power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid wasting material — every part must be used to advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: Material that is amassed but not used weakens the book; 'great masses of that life are being wasted' when scenes do not serve the central plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prune or repurpose episodes and details so that each contributes to the theme, form, or dramatic progression of the novel; do not leave large unused reserves that divide or dilute effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show rather than merely state — the novel must look true within itself
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel is not merely a row of facts or an argument to be attested externally; 'the thing has to look true' by its internal methods rather than by outside assertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor methods that make the book itself authoritative (dramatisation, pictorial rendering, point-of-view) rather than relying on reported truth or external attestation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice and management of method: scenic vs panoramic presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between 'scenic' (particular scenes, an immediate hour) and 'panoramic' (surveying lives from a height) presentation; both are legitimate but different methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide when to place the reader directly in a scene and when to step back for a general view; manage shifts so they are motivated and consistent with the subject, using summaries to prepare scenes when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial voice and impersonality — how the author's presence is handled
rubrics_metrics.description: An author may be 'impersonal' in style yet still embody opinions through dramatization; the writer's voice sometimes speaks directly and sometimes through characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be conscious whether you're presenting material in the author's own voice or through a character's perception; dramatize opinions rather than stating them bluntly, unless deliberate authorial comment is intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of view management — whose consciousness frames the scene
rubrics_metrics.description: The point of view may be the author's omniscience, the mind of a character, or shifts between them; this determines the colouring and judgment applied to events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose and handle point-of-view shifts deliberately (e.g., render a landscape as the author sees it or as it appears to Emma); ensure shifts serve the book's design and do not jar the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pictorial (subjective) vs dramatic (objective) treatment of scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: A scene can be pictorial—bathed in a character's mood and not transferable to the stage—or dramatic—presented as visible and audible facts that could be staged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether the scene's main effect depends on interior colouring (pictorial) or on observable action and dialogue (dramatic), and render it in the appropriate mode to preserve the intended effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial intervention: when to supply background or penetrate consciousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes the author must intervene to supply past facts or disclose unexpressed thought because surface detail alone is insufficient for understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use authorial intervention sparingly and purposefully: provide necessary background or interior access when essential for meaning, but balance it against showing through scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixing methods consistently and within a guiding principle
rubrics_metrics.description: A novelist may use many devices (scenic, panoramic, pictorial, dramatic, authorial intrusion) but must be 'consistent on some plan' and allow only the latitude required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish the governing principle or plan for mixing methods and adhere to it so variety enhances rather than fragments the reader's sense of the whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation and necessity of scenes — every scene must do specific work
rubrics_metrics.description: A scene that is not prepared or that 'does nothing in particular' is a weakness; scenes should be placed where they will 'thoroughly illuminate' the subject and advance action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each scene is motivated by preceding material and prepares or fulfills an effect for which the narrative has set the stage; remove or revise scenes that fail to make their intended effect.
